title: Positivity of the separator's total weight
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$, let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ be a payoff function, and let $u$ be a finite sample of columns drawn from $Y$. Suppose $X$ is nonempty, fix a vector $c \in \bbr^u$, and let $L : \bbr^u \to \bbr$ be a continuous linear functional that strictly separates $c$ from the finite upper image $U(X,f,u)$, in the sense that $L(z) < L(c)$ for every $z \in U(X,f,u)$. Writing $e_y \in \bbr^u$ for the standard basis vector supported at coordinate $y$, one then has
\[
  0 \;<\; \sum_{y \in u} \bigl(-L(e_y)\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a continuous linear functional on $\bbr^u$
$L$ strictly separates $c$ from the finite upper image: $L(z) < L(c)$ for all $z \in U(X,f,u)$
replaced:
Under the same separation hypothesis, with $X$ nonempty,
\[
  0 \;<\; \sum_{y \in u} \bigl(-L(e_y)\bigr).
\]
Consequently the negated coordinates can be normalized to a probability vector on
the sampled columns.
